headline: Nikon photography contest winner stripped of title after AI use confirmed
summary: Dr. Ning Xu's award-winning microscopic video was found to contain AI-generated elements, leading to disqualification and a review of contest rules.
details: The winner of Nikon's 16th annual Small World in Motion contest, Dr. Ning Xu, has had his title revoked. His microscopic video, initially lauded, was found to contain AI-generated elements, raising concerns within the scientific community about the integrity of the competition.

Concerns were first raised by researchers who noted abnormalities in the video's cellular structures, with some features appearing and disappearing unnaturally. These anomalies are considered classic indicators of AI generation in visual media.

Further evidence emerged when a PhD student identified a distinctive watermark on the source image, strongly suggesting AI involvement. Two former competition judges also voiced doubts about the video's authenticity.

In a now-deleted LinkedIn post, Dr. Xu admitted to using AI during post-processing to enhance visualization, but insisted it did not generate the video itself or the depicted cellular movement. He claimed he had not violated competition rules.
However, Nikon's investigation concluded that Xu had indeed violated the contest's rules. The top prize has now been awarded to Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam for his video of microscopic organisms.

This incident follows a trend of AI-generated content winning art and photography competitions. Nikon has stated it plans to "revisit rules and evaluation procedures for future competition entries" to prevent similar occurrences.

headline_marked: [[Digital Dissident Devroom]] at FOSDEM aims to fight censorship
headline: Digital Dissident Devroom at FOSDEM aims to fight censorship
summary: A new devroom at FOSDEM 2027 will focus on building tools to resist censorship and protect digital freedom.
details: The Digital Dissident Devroom at FOSDEM 2027 is being organized to foster collaboration on tools that combat censorship and protect digital freedoms globally. The initiative aims to bring together developers, researchers, and activists to create trustworthy and controllable communication technologies.

The devroom's focus is on the complete chain of tools individuals use to communicate safely, expose truth, and resist surveillance, particularly for those living under authoritarian regimes. It emphasizes the need for interoperability and a holistic understanding of security, acknowledging that the weakest link can compromise the entire system.

Unlike other devrooms that focus on specific technologies like decentralization or privacy, Digital Dissident centers on the user under threat and the end-to-end toolchains that protect them. This approach addresses the complex, multi-tool strategies required for daily security in restrictive environments.

The need for this dedicated space is highlighted by the increasing sophistication of censorship tactics, including allow-listing, protocol fingerprinting, and app store removals. Developers have responded with various solutions, but progress remains fragmented, necessitating a unified approach to share threat models and engineering practices.

FOSDEM 2027 will feature a mix of formats designed to engage participants, with organizers prioritizing technical merit and a balanced representation of projects, regions, and speakers. Each presentation will require an explicit threat model and an honest account of limitations.
